newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end at 22-month high, plastics soar.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end at 22-month high, plastics soar.

text.p: Taiwan share prices ended at a 22-month high on Wednesday, pushed higher for a third straight session as buying interest shifted to the plastics sector and conglomerate shares, brokers said.
The weighted index finished up 41.48 points or 0.62 percent to 6,729.36, its highest close since January 11, 1995, but back from the bullish session's intraday high of 6,764.65.
Turnover was an active T$81.27 billion.
The upward momentum was fuelled in part by what brokers called politically motivated, state-linked buying marking six months since President Lee Teng-hui's inauguration.

Lee, a landslide victor in March in Taiwan's first direct presidential election, was sworn in on May 20 and urged state agencies at the time to boost investment in six months. Brokers said state funds appeared to be taking his appeal seriously.
"Recent stock market rises inspire an overall optimism. Amid abundant liquidity, funds are flowing into the stock market," Joe Chiou, an analyst of Taiwan Securities Investment, said.

Plastics led the market surge, gaining 2.71 percent on word of Formosa group's plans for a big U.S. petrochemical expansion. Three key members of the group, Taiwan's top industrial combine, all rose. Nan Ya Plastics jumped T$3.5 or 6.54 percent to T$57.
Computer giant Acer Inc, the session's most active issue, was up T$1.4 or 3.27 percent to T$44.2, while the entire electronics and machinery sector up 0.93 percent.
Textile shares gained 1.13 percent, but the heavily weighted financials slipped 0.21 percent.
Brokers said the rally was showing signs of flagging.
"Unless there is more bullish news, profit-taking pressure is due to emerge soon," Chiou said.
A range of 6,680-6,750 was seen for Thursday.
